findings.title: Public findMany() method removed and return types changed without updating/verifying callers
findings.body: The service previously exposed `findMany(findManyArgs)` which executed a Prisma ORM query and returned typed rows, and `getAuthorizationConditions()/getFilterConditions()` returned `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` objects. In this PR `findMany` is removed entirely and those methods now return `Prisma.Sql` fragments instead, replaced only by `getBaseConditions()` which returns a raw SQL fragment that the caller must manually embed in a `$queryRaw` call. The 2-file diff in this PR contains no updates to any consumer of `InsightsBookingService` (e.g. tRPC routers or other services that likely call `.findMany()` or rely on the old where-object return type). If any such caller exists outside this diff, it will fail to compile/run after this change. This is a breaking API change that should be verified against all current consumers before merge.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests were deleted instead of updated
findings.body: The previous test suite included a `describe("Caching", ...)` block with two tests ("should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions") that verified `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` caching logic. This PR removes that entire block rather than updating the assertions to the new `Prisma.Sql` comparison style. The caching implementation (`getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` memoization) still exists in `insightsBooking.ts`, but there is now no test coverage verifying that repeated calls reuse the cached SQL fragment instead of rebuilding them (which would re-run DB membership/team lookups). This leaves a regression gap for future changes to the caching logic.

findings.title: PR description misrepresents scope of changes to production service code
findings.body: The PR description states the Prisma.sql conversion "was previously converted in the service implementation" and that this PR "updates... integration tests" only, implying `insightsBooking.ts` is unchanged production code being re-verified. However the diff shows `insightsBooking.ts` itself undergoes a full rewrite in this PR: changing the import of `Prisma` from type-only to value import, replacing the `findMany` method with `getBaseConditions`, changing `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` return types from Prisma where-objects to `Prisma.Sql`, and changing the constructor's accepted options type. This mismatch between the stated scope (test-only) and the actual scope (significant production logic + API changes) risks reviewers under-scrutinizing the new authorization/filter SQL-building logic, despite the PR's own checklist flagging it as "HIGH RISK".

findings.title: Unreachable fallback branches in getBaseConditions due to buildAuthorizationConditions never returning falsy
findings.body: `getBaseConditions()` branches on `if (authConditions && filterConditions) ... else if (authConditions) ... else if (filterConditions) ... else return NOTHING_CONDITION`. However `buildAuthorizationConditions()` (and thus `getAuthorizationConditions()`) always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null/undefined), so `authConditions` is always truthy. The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches are therefore dead code that can mask a future contract change (e.g. if `getAuthorizationConditions` is later made to return null in some case, the fallback behavior silently differs from what a reader would expect).
